mcat_description.short: Cattle Sheds are prefabricated or semi-permanent farm structures designed to house dairy cattle (cows, buffaloes), goats, and other livestock, typically built with mild steel or galvanised steel frames and corrugated roofing sheets. They are sold as complete supply-and-erect solutions or as fabricated structural kits, customised to herd size and farm layout.
mcat_description.long: Cattle Sheds in the Indian B2B market are purpose-built livestock housing structures supplied by fabricators and pre-engineered building contractors, primarily serving commercial dairy farmers, small-scale livestock entrepreneurs, and agri-entrepreneurs setting up new farms. The dominant construction system uses mild steel or galvanised steel structural frames with corrugated GI, PPGI, or fibre-cement roofing sheets, concrete or brick-paved flooring with drainage slopes, and open or semi-open side walls to ensure ventilation — consistent with BIS recommendations for loose housing systems across most Indian agro-climatic zones. Buyers typically specify shed dimensions (length × width in feet), herd capacity (number of animals), roofing material, flooring type, and ancillary features such as water troughs, mangers, and drainage channels. A significant sub-segment covers elevated slatted-floor goat sheds, which use a raised wooden or metal platform design distinct from ground-level cattle housing.

market_context: Cattle Sheds in India are primarily supplied as prefabricated or semi-permanent steel-framed structures by small-to-medium fabricators and pre-engineered building (PEB) contractors, with Rajasthan, Bihar, Tamil Nadu, and Maharashtra emerging as key supplier geographies based on listing distribution signals. The Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) has published space and housing recommendations for dairy cattle under ISI standards, with the loose housing system recommended for most Indian agro-climatic zones — this is the dominant design paradigm for commercial dairy farms. Relevant Indian standards for roofing materials include IS 459 (corrugated cement sheets) and IS 3007 (laying of corrugated roofing), which are referenced by Indian roofing manufacturers for cattle shed applications. The market spans two distinct buyer tiers: small/marginal farmers seeking low-cost sheds for 5–20 animals, and commercial dairy entrepreneurs setting up 50–200+ head operations who require turnkey design-and-build solutions with milking parlour integration, drainage systems, and water troughs. Goat farming sheds — particularly elevated slatted-floor designs — represent a growing sub-segment driven by expanding small ruminant farming across Rajasthan, UP, and MP. Asia-Pacific, including India, shows the fastest growth rate in prefabricated livestock building adoption, driven by expanding domestic dairy and meat markets (single source — low confidence for growth rate claim). Key buyer decision factors are shed size/dimensions, structural material (MS vs GI vs SS), roofing type, herd capacity, ventilation design, and total construction cost per sq ft.
